speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Here's the problem with teleportation.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Lay it on me.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Assuming the device could be invented which would identify the quantum state of matter of an individual in one location, and transmit that pattern to a distant location for reassembly, you would not have actually transported the individual. You would have destroyed him in one location, and recreated him in another.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: How about that.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Personally, I would never use a transporter. Because the original Sheldon would have to be disintegrated in order to create a new Sheldon.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Would the new Sheldon be in any way an improvement on the old Sheldon?

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: No, he would be exactly the same.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: That is a problem.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: So, you see it too.

speaker: dr_eric_gablehauser
text: Dr Hofstadter, Dr Cooper.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Gablehouser.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Gablehouser.

speaker: dr_eric_gablehauser
text: Gentlemen, I'd like you to meet Dennis Kim. Dennis is a highly sought after Doctorial candidate and we're hoping to have him do his graduate work here.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Graduate work, very impressive.

speaker: dr_eric_gablehauser
text: And he's only fifteen years old.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Not bad, I myself started graduate school at fourteen.

speaker: dennis_kim
text: Well, I lost a year while my family was tunnelling out of North Korea.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Advantage Kim.

speaker: dr_eric_gablehauser
text: I thought maybe you boys could show Dennis around, let him see why we're the best physics research facility in the country.

speaker: dennis_kim
text: I already know you're not. You don't have an open science grid computer, or a free electron laser, and the string theory research being done here is nothing but a dead end.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Excuse me, that is my research, and it is by no means a dead end.

speaker: dennis_kim
text: Well, obviously you don't see it yet, but trust me, you will.

speaker: dr_eric_gablehauser
text: Dennis, we discussed this, we're in the process of updating our equipment, and we welcome your input on our research goals, and we' ve agreed to look the other way if you want to use up to 20% of the grant money you attract to smuggle your grandfather out of Pyongyang. We want him here boys, make it happen.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Yes sir.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: You can count on us, we're on it. What the hell do you mean, dead end.

speaker: dennis_kim
text: I mean, the whole landscape of false vacuums in string theory could be as large as ten to the five- hundredth power. In addition... ooh, look, chocolate milk.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I sense a disturbance in the force.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: A bad feeling I have about this, mmm- hmmm.
